skills.name: benchmarking
skills.description: Guide for building, running, and analyzing Nanvix performance benchmarks. Use this when asked about benchmark setup, execution, or interpretation.

skills.name: build
skills.description: Guide for building, formatting, linting, and spell-checking Nanvix with z. Use this when asked to build or validate the repository.

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline
skills.description: Guide for Nanvix CI and GitHub Actions workflow behavior, including local pipeline execution and matrix coverage. Use this when asked about CI checks, workflow failures, or release flow.

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development
skills.description: Guide for developing and debugging Nanvix daemons, including guest daemons and host linuxd behavior. Use this when asked about daemon architecture or daemon changes.

skills.name: gdb-debugging
skills.description: Guide for debugging Nanvix guests using GDB remote debugging over the microvm machine type. Use this when asked about attaching GDB, setting breakpoints, or stepping through kernel code.

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development
skills.description: Guide for creating and modifying Nanvix libraries under src/libs, including guest no_std and host std crates. Use this when asked about library architecture or crate changes.

skills.name: test-development
skills.description: Guide for writing, running, and debugging Nanvix unit, integration, and system tests in Rust and C/C++. Use this when asked about test implementation or failures.

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: troubleshooting
skills.description: Guide for diagnosing Nanvix build, runtime, and test failures, including cleanup and debugging workflows. Use this when asked to investigate errors or unstable behavior.

skills.name: user-app-development
skills.description: Guide for developing, building, and running Nanvix user-space applications across supported runtimes and languages. Use this when asked about guest app implementation or execution.

skills.name: find-skills
skills.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

skills.name: customize-cloud-agent
skills.description: Skill for customizing the Copilot cloud agent (formerly known as Copilot coding agent) environment, including copilot-setup-steps.yml configuration, preinstalling tools and dependencies, runners, and settings. Use when the user mentions copilot-setup-steps, copilot setup steps, or wants to configure the cloud agent environment.

4. // KernelFrame - Specifications
5. //
6. // `KernelFrame` is an owned, move-only RAII handle to a single page-sized
7. // physical frame allocated for kernel use and identity-mapped into the kernel
8. // address space. Its abstract value is exactly the base physical address of the
9. // frame it owns (`KernelFrame@ : int`, defined by the `View` impl in
10. // `kframe.rs`). No caller inspects storage layout; frames are named purely
11. // through `@` / `base()`.
12. //
13. // All mutable allocator state (which frames are allocated, per-frame refcounts)
14. // lives in the do-not-modify `FrameAllocView` reached through `phys_view()`
15. // (`mod.spec.rs`). Because `phys_view()` is a zero-argument uninterpreted spec
16. // function (a single fixed value at the current program point), the `Drop`
17. // effect is expressed as a monotone single-state fact over `phys_view()`,
18. // exactly like the `frame::free` shim contract -- there is no
19. // `old(phys_view())` to state a before/after transition against.
20. 
21. verus! {
22. 
23. // Bring the global physical-memory view into scope so the `Drop` contract in
24. // `kframe.rs` can state invariant preservation over `phys_view()`.
25. use crate::mm::phys::phys_view;
26. 
27. // `<PageAligned<PhysicalAddress> as Address>::from_raw_value` is a trait method
28. // of the external `sys::mm::Address` trait, below this module's verification
29. // boundary. `KernelFrame::new` calls it only to obtain the page-aligned physical
30. // address it then identity-maps; no abstract `mm::phys` fact depends on the
31. // returned value, so a trivial trusted contract suffices to make the call
32. // verifiable. Replaced when `hal::mem` is verified.
33. pub assume_specification<T: crate::hal::mem::Address> [
34.     <crate::hal::mem::PageAligned<T> as crate::hal::mem::Address>::from_raw_value
35. ](raw_addr: usize) -> (result: Result<
36.     crate::hal::mem::PageAligned<T>,
37.     ::sys::error::Error,
38. >);
39. 
40. } // verus!
41.

2. // Licensed under the MIT License.
3. 
4. // KernelFrame - Proofs
5. //
6. // No proof lemmas are required for `new` / `base` / `drop`: the address-identity
7. // of `new` follows directly from the `View` impl, `base` is a trivial accessor,
8. // and the `Drop` invariant-preservation guarantee is provided verbatim by the

1. // Copyright(c) The Maintainers of Nanvix.
2. // Licensed under the MIT License.
3. 
4. //! Kernel frame type.
5. //!
6. //! A [`KernelFrame`] represents a single page-sized physical frame allocated for kernel use.
7. //! It provides `Deref`/`DerefMut` for direct kernel access (identity-mapped) and frees the
8. //! underlying frame on drop via the global frame allocator.
9. 
10. //==================================================================================================
11. // Imports
12. //==================================================================================================
13. 
14. use vstd::prelude::*;
15. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
16. include!("kframe.spec.rs");
17. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
18. include!("kframe.proof.rs");
19. 
20. use crate::hal::mem::{
21.     Address,
22.     FrameAddress,
23.     PageAligned,
24.     PhysicalAddress,
25. };
26. use ::arch::mem;
27. use ::core::ops::{
28.     Deref,
29.     DerefMut,
30. };
31. use ::sys::error::Error;
32. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
33. use ::vstd::prelude::*;
34. 
35. //==================================================================================================
36. // Kernel Frame
37. //==================================================================================================
38. 
39. /// A type that represents a kernel frame.
40. #[derive(Debug)]
41. #[verus_verify]
42. pub struct KernelFrame {
43.     /// Frame address.
44.     base: FrameAddress,
45. }
46. 
47. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
48. verus! {
49. 
50. /// Abstract view of a [`KernelFrame`]: the base physical address of the frame it
51. /// owns. Lets allocator contracts name a returned kernel frame's address (e.g.
52. /// the contiguity guarantee of `alloc_many_kernel_frames`) without exposing any
53. /// storage detail.
54. impl View for KernelFrame {
55.     type V = int;
56. 
57.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> int {
58.         self.base@
59.     }
60. }
61. 
62. } // verus!
63. 
64. #[verus_verify]
65. impl KernelFrame {
66.     ///
67.     /// # Description
68.     ///
69.     /// Instantiates a kernel frame.
70.     ///
71.     /// # Parameters
72.     ///
73.     /// - `base`: Frame address.
74.     ///
75.     /// # Returns
76.     ///
77.     /// Upon success, a kernel frame is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
78.     ///
79.     #[verus_spec(result =>
80.         ensures
81.             // Address identity: on success the handle owns exactly the input
82.             // address, so callers can transfer the allocator facts established
83.             // for `base` (membership, alignment) onto the returned handle. On
84.             // failure no handle exists; `base` is `Copy`, so nothing is consumed
85.             // and the caller remains free to release the raw frame.
86.             match result {
87.                 Ok(frame) => frame@ == base@,
88.                 Err(_) => true,
89.             },
90.     )]
91.     pub(super) fn new(base: FrameAddress) -> Result<Self, Error> {
92.         // Ensure the frame is identity-mapped in the kernel address space so that
93.         // Deref/DerefMut can safely access it. This lazily installs a page
94.         // table entry if needed (page tables come from a BSS pool, so no recursive frame
95.         // allocation occurs).
96.         let phys_addr: PageAligned<PhysicalAddress> =
97.             PageAligned::from_raw_value(base.into_raw_value()).map_err(|e| {
98.                 error!("frame base is not page-aligned: {e:?}");
99.                 e
100.             })?;
101.         crate::mm::virt::identity_map_page(phys_addr).map_err(|e| {
102.             error!("failed to identity-map frame: {:?}", e);
103.             e
104.         })?;
105. 
106.         Ok(Self { base })
107.     }
108. 
109.     ///
110.     /// # Description
111.     ///
112.     /// Returns the base address of the target kernel frame.
113.     ///
114.     /// # Returns
115.     ///
116.     /// The base address of the target kernel frame.
117.     ///
118.     #[verus_spec(result =>
119.         ensures
120.             // Pure read: the returned address is the handle's abstract value.
121.             result@ == self@,
122.     )]
123.     pub fn base(&self) -> FrameAddress {
124.         self.base
125.     }
126. 
127.     ///
128.     /// # Description
129.     ///
130.     /// Clears the target kernel frame.
131.     ///
132.     /// Uses the identity-map `memset` backend so that the write runs in the kernel address space.
133.     /// This avoids a page fault when the current CR3 points to a user page directory that lacks
134.     /// the PDE for this frame's physical address.
135.     ///
136.     // Trusted (TCB, out of verification scope): materializes a `*mut u8` from the
137.     // frame's raw address (`usize as *mut u8`) and writes through the identity-map
138.     // `memset` backend -- a raw-memory operation Verus cannot model. Listed in
139.     // `verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md`.
140.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
141.     pub fn clear(&mut self) -> Result<(), Error> {
142.         let base: *mut u8 = self.base.into_raw_value() as *mut u8;
143.         crate::mm::virt::memset(base, 0, mem::PAGE_SIZE).map_err(|e| {
144.             error!("memset failed: {:?}", e);
145.             e
146.         })
147.     }
148. }
149. 
150. /// # Safety
151. ///
152. /// `Deref` accesses the identity-mapped frame directly. The caller must ensure that the current
153. /// CR3 points to a page directory that has the relevant PDE for this frame's physical address
154. /// (i.e., the kernel page directory, or a user page directory into which the PDE has been
155. /// propagated via [`sync_kernel_pdes`](crate::mm::virt::sync_kernel_pdes)). For CR3-agnostic
156. /// writes, prefer [`KernelFrame::clear()`] which uses the identity-map `memset` backend.
157. impl Deref for KernelFrame {
158.     type Target = [u8];
159. 
160.     fn deref(&self) -> &Self::Target {
161.         let ptr: usize = self.base.into_raw_value();
162.         unsafe { core::slice::from_raw_parts(ptr as *const u8, mem::PAGE_SIZE) }
163.     }
164. }
165. 
166. /// # Safety
167. ///
168. /// See [`Deref`] impl — the same CR3 invariant applies.
169. impl DerefMut for KernelFrame {
170.     fn deref_mut(&mut self) -> &mut Self::Target {
171.         let ptr: usize = self.base.into_raw_value();
172.         unsafe { core::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(ptr as *mut u8, mem::PAGE_SIZE) }
173.     }
174. }
175. 
176. #[verus_verify]
177. impl Drop for KernelFrame {
178.     #[verus_spec(
179.         ensures
180.             // Releasing the frame preserves the subsystem invariant (the last
181.             // reference returns the frame to the free pool). The precise refcount
182.             // transition is not expressible: `phys_view()` is a single fixed value
183.             // with no `old(phys_view())` to compare against. Errors are logged, not
184.             // propagated, so `drop` cannot unwind.
185.             phys_view().inv(),
186.         opens_invariants none
187.         no_unwind
188.     )]
189.     fn drop(&mut self) {
190.         if let Err(e) = super::frame::free(self.base) {
191.             error!("failed to free kernel frame: {:?}", e);
192.         }
193.     }
194. }
